kevin: quick note — spotted reproducible memory growth in kvcache paged mode on MI250 during longctx runs (8192+). pattern: per-iteration resident grows ~18-22MB.
kevin: repro: ./run_repro.sh --model pagedattn --gpu mi250 --seq 8192 --batch 1 --iters 2000
kevin: logs snippet:
```
[evict] freed 0 spans, pending=3
[pt] unmap_span id=0x7f... refs=0 -> expected free, but resid remains
memory: rss 2.1G -> 2.12G -> 2.14G ...
```
maria: can you paste the runtime commit and PT counters? also did you try h100?
kevin: runtime: a1b2c3d (kv-pager-async-evict). PT counters:
```
pt_allocs=1245
pt_unmaps=1239
pt_ref_inc=5678
pt_ref_dec=5676
```
kevin: so dec < inc by 2 consistently.
alex: interesting — on H100 i saw similar fragmentation but no leak. eviction latency spiked at ~7ms when coalescing ran.
sarah: i added a debug flush (FORCE_PT_FLUSH=1) and the leak stops but tail latency doubles. not ideal.
kevin: traced with ftrace: async_evict cb runs on completion thread; path: evict -> coalesce_spans -> remap_to_shadow -> dec_ref -> maybe_free. race window when remap and free overlap.
maria: hypothesis: refcount decrement path sometimes skipped if remap path takes alternate branch (hw dma mapping) on MI250.
alex: can you try with env FORCE_SYNC_EVICT=1? that'll serialize and should show if race is the cause.
kevin: ran with FORCE_SYNC_EVICT=1 — growth gone. numbers back to stable. so it's a concurrency race.
kevin: stack trace from repro (condensed):
```
evict_worker+0x47
coalesce_spans+0x130
remap_to_shadow+0x88
kvcache_ref_dec+0x24
kvcache_free_span+0x90
```
maria: ok let's pick this up in a small repro harness and add assertions to PT ref ops. alex+kevin pair to debug hardware diff (h100 vs mi250) — maybe driver DMA ordering differs.
kevin: I'll open a PR w/ repro, ftrace script, and a small patch gating async evict behind opt-in flag. assigning myself + alex. ticket: INF-3421
sarah: :thumbsup: please add perf test to CI on both h100 and mi250.
deploy-bot: created ticket INF-3421 and linked CI job run/kvcache-longctx-repro.
alex: also add telemetry counters for pt_inc/pt_dec per-gpu; that will make future triage easier.
kevin: will do. thanks team :eyes:
